name: gp-v18
notes: gp-v17 plus the controller configuration object (System FW 0x805B7480+0x1E0, pointer in .sbss
0x805A00C8): after the per-port button layouts it keeps per-port stick state that the main thread
updates every frame (fn_8004897C, the stick conversion, and P+'s hook in it at 0x80579398 write
flags at 0x805B75DA/DB). A resimulated frame read the flags the first run had left (0x41 instead
of 0x01), and in a Donkey Kong mirror P1's air drift started 5 frames later than in play without
rollback (game frame 5644, x -16.24 against -16.28). The layouts are constant during a match. The
granule 0x805B7640-0x805B7680 also holds the start of the next block (a thread stack's bottom with
its 0xDEADBABE marker): those 32 bytes are excluded.
--- gp-v17 notes ---
gp-v16 plus all of lbl_80494E00 (0xE8) and lbl_80494EE8 (0x2D8), DOL .bss 0x80494E00-0x804951C0:
records the scene code keeps per model (fn_8000E214, fn_8000EB1C, fn_8000F4F0 from
gfTaskScheduler::render; fn_80024E50), with pointers into the fighters' resource heaps and instance
heaps. dolw-g1 restored only two of their granules (0x80494F20+0x40, 0x80494FA0+0x20). A Zelda/Sheik
transformation swaps the fighter's model resource (0x915712A0 <-> 0x915FB960); after a rollback across
it a record pointed at the other form's resource while the heap held this one, and the render
called through garbage (main thread at 0x20, lr 0x8019D990 in fn_8019D950, as in the Meta Knight
hangs). Now the records are restored whole, with the heaps they point into.
--- gp-v16 notes ---
gp-v15 plus the archive manager (gfArchiveManager in System FW at 0x805BB860, *g_gfArchiveManager
(.sbss 0x8059FFA0): {count, first, last} of every loaded gfArchive, and a second list). Its nodes are
the gfArchive objects in the heaps the archives were loaded into (fighter resources, Effect, item
resources: in the set); the head was not. An archive loaded or released in a rolled-back frame (a
Zelda/Sheik transformation's FitSheik00.pac / FitSheikMotionEtc.pac, Pokemon and Assist Trophy
preloads) left the head pointing at the discarded run's archive, and the re-created archive was
linked to itself; 'File Clone' (gfArchive::update looks an archive up by name in this list) and the
fighter's resource setup then worked on the wrong data (the transformed fighter's position read as
pointers, 'changeStatus on a non-existent article').
--- gp-v15 notes ---
gp-v14 plus the file IO manager's bookkeeping (System FW, the same addresses on every boot;
g_gfFileIOManager .sbss 0x8059FFF4 -> 0x805CA1C0): its two request queues (utQueue 0x805BF860, queue
0x805BFAA0, utQueue 0x805BFAE0, queue 0x805BFD20), the request pool (bitmap 0x805BFD60, 128
gfFileIORequest of 0xA4 bytes from 0x805BFD74, pool header 0x805C4FA0) and the manager (0x805CA1C0
+0x9C). Mid-match loads (a Zelda/Sheik transformation reads the other form's motion and model files
into the fighter's resource heap; items preload Pokemon and Assist Trophy resources) allocate
requests that the game holds for some frames: without the pool, a rollback across a request left the
game's handles pointing at requests the pool had freed or given to another load. Needs the session's
file IO wait (GameplaySession.cpp RunIoWait): at every loop top the main thread waits until no
request is queued, so the IO thread is idle at every save and load and these bytes are quiescent.
Not the IO thread itself (its gfThread/OSThread at 0x805BF4E0 and its stack).
--- gp-v14 notes ---
gp-v13 plus the camera subject list head (cmSubjectList, DOL .bss lbl_8049DEDC: {count, first, last};
getSubjectByPlayerNo__13cmSubjectListFUl, fn_8009EC5C, fn_8009C38C). Its nodes are the camera
subjects of fighters and items (Smash Balls, other items), in the instance heaps (in the set); the
head was not. A rolled-back frame that created or removed a subject (an item spawning or vanishing,
a fighter instance changing at a Zelda/Sheik transformation) left the head pointing at the discarded
run's nodes: the re-created node ended up linked to itself (the camera ignored that subject, so the
camera, the Smash Ball's flight inside the camera range and then the RNG drifted from play without
rollback: sweep Family D), or the list formed a cycle (the main thread looping in fn_8009EFCC <-
fn_8009EC5C: Family A's hangs). Whole granules 0x8049DEC0-0x8049DF00 are restored; the rest of
them (a pointer at 0x8049DEC8, the static destructor entry 0x8049DED0, constant tag codes from
0x8049DEE8) does not change during a match.
--- gp-v13 notes ---
gp-v12 minus nw4r::ef's draw strategies (DOL .bss 0x804A3E90+0x578, lbl_804A3E90): seven function-local
statics of fn_80174434 (the draw-strategy getter), each built on first use behind a guard byte in .sbss
(0x805A04F0..0x805A04F6, outside the set). dolw-g1 restored some of their granules, among them the
vtable of strategy 1 (0x804A3F64). When the first effect drawn with that strategy appeared in a frame
that was rolled back, the load zeroed the object again while its guard stayed set, so it was never
rebuilt; the next draw (fn_801638D0 -> fn_8016DE08) called through its zero vtable and the main thread
jumped to 0x20 (sweep Family B: early hangs in the Yoshi, Dedede, G&W, R.O.B., Ice Climbers, Knuckles
and Lucas mirrors, lr 0x80163918). The strategies are rendering state only; now neither they nor their
guards are restored.
--- gp-v12 notes ---
gp-v11 plus the camera quake controller (System FW block at 0x805B69C0, object 0x805B69E0+0x280,
reached through the .sbss pointer 0x805A0280; cmReqQuake__FiP5Vec3f -> fn_8009D564). A quake request
sets a flag at +0x270 (and its amplitude at +0x268). A frame that requested a quake and was rolled
back left the flag set, so the resimulation took the 'quake already running' path and shook the
camera differently; for the quake's 11 frames the fighters' checksum differed between first run
and resimulation (sync tests: Ice Climbers/Olimar, R.O.B./Olimar, Ice Climbers/Charizard). Found
by replaying a sync test's passes and tracing the burst frame's first run against its
resimulation (gprb_mispredict.py --trace-frame, PPR_GPRB_INTERP_FROM).
--- gp-v11 notes ---
gp-v10 plus the ground-collision object lists in DOL .bss (0x8049E570..0x8049E5A0: lbl_8049E570,
g_grCollisionList 0x8049E57C, lbl_8049E588, lbl_8049E594; the lists are {count, sentinel next,
sentinel prev}, 0x8049E570/0x8049E588 are their static destructor-chain entries). The nodes
(ground-collision objects) live in the fighters' heaps, in the set; the heads did not. A rolled-back
frame that created such an object left the head pointing at the discarded run's node; the re-run
linked the object to itself and iteration skipped it. Peers with different rollbacks diverged
(dual-core Mario/Marth FD sessions), and even a plain sync test drifted from the game without
rollback (Mario/Marth FD, game frame 312), unseen because both runs of a frame shared the corruption.
Whole granules 0x8049E540-0x8049E5C0 are restored; the bytes beside the lists stay zero in a match.
Also the last record of the array at 0x8049EDE0 (lbl_8049EDD8, entries pointing into the Effect
heap): dolw-g1 restored it only up to 0x8049EE40.
--- gp-v10 notes ---
gp-v9 plus the whole global slow-motion manager (gf_slow_manager.o: the requests in .bss
0x804953B0+0x20, s_needsUpdate in .sbss 0x805A0080, s_maxSlowRate in .sdata 0x8059C690): a slow
request made by a mispredicted run stayed active after the rollback. And 'exclude': loads restore whole 64-byte granules, so a
range that starts or ends inside a granule took the rest of it along. The System heap starts at
0x80611F60, inside the granule that holds the last 32 bytes of the GX FIFO ring (RenderFifo,
CP FIFO end 0x80611F40): a load wrote stale commands into the ring, and the GPU then ran them
(missing draw-done interrupts, GXWaitDrawDone hangs, garbage indexed-XF loads). Excluded bytes are
never written by a load.
gp-v8 plus gfCameraManager (0x805B6D20+0x740, allocated in System FW at boot, the same
address on every boot; pointer at r13-0x4460 = 0x8059FFC0). The camera's state lived outside the
set, so a resimulated frame started from the newer camera; the cameras of two peers drifted apart
with their different rollback histories. In dual-core sessions this changed gameplay (a fighter
near the edge of the screen took 1% on one peer only: off-screen damage depends on the camera).
gp-v7 plus two areas P+ uses for its own data, outside every heap: 0x935F0000+0x1000 (high
MEM2 above the last heap: per-port input buffers and counters of P+ codes) and
0x805A7400+0x2000 (the never-used bottom of the boot stack: P+ scratch, including the pad
struct at 0x805A9338 that the game's controller conversion reads). A resimulated frame read
the newer input there.
gp-v6 plus the Replay heap (the replay recorder's buffers and counters, which the input code
reads back every frame) and the main thread's outer stack frames above the game loop
(main/mainLoop locals stay live across iterations; one is a frame counter the input code
reads at 0x805B50D8). Below the loop's stack pointer the stack is dead at the loop top.
gp-v5 with the WiiPad heap back, together with the object that owns its lists (0x805B62A0 in
System FW, next to AreaManager): the main thread's pad manager (fn_8001750C -> fn_8002C614)
keeps per-frame state in WiiPad, and a resimulated frame read the newer values. gp-v3 had
dropped WiiPad because restoring its nodes without the owner's list heads made a cycle; both
halves are restored now. Only the main thread writes either (all-threads trace).
gp-v4 plus the gfTaskScheduler object (list heads, pending list) and the one gfTask outside the
set (AreaManager, its links): tasks live in set heaps but their list heads live in System FW.
Restoring the nodes without the heads, after tasks were created or removed in the rolled-back
frames, left a cycle and gfTaskScheduler::process never returned.
gp-v3 plus the input history the main thread derives every frame, and small globals that only
the main thread writes during a match (found with an all-threads interpreter trace of 15
frames after GO: main-thread stores outside the set, minus stack, render and sound memory).
Without the pad history a resimulated frame computed 'pressed this frame' against the newest
frame's pads and diverged as soon as a button was pressed.
gp-v2 minus the WiiPad heap: it holds list nodes of a pad manager whose list heads live in
System FW (outside the set, walked by fn_8001750C every main-loop pass). Restoring the nodes
alone linked them into a cycle and the main thread spun forever with interrupts off. Input
is injected per frame (Gprb::Pads), so the pad plumbing is not rollback state.
gp-v1 minus 0x80493EC0+0x40: that granule is the C stdio FILE table (__files, 0x80493E60
+0x140), written by whichever thread prints (OSReport). Restoring it under other threads'
prints broke __fwrite (main thread hung in __memrchr with a trashed stack). Not gameplay.
Gameplay region set for gameplay-only (Slippi-style) rollback, from the feasibility spike
(docs/gameplay-rollback-feasibility.md, Experiment 3). Heaps are resolved by name from the live
heap table (g_HeapInfos 0x80494958) at the start of the match; rel_data adds the data and bss
sections of every loaded REL (OS module list 0x800030C8). 'add' entries are static ranges:
[effective address, size, label]. 'remove' punches holes: [address, size, label].
Not in the set on purpose: OS state (lowmem, stacks, SystemFW, thread/alarm state in .bss),
audio (Sound heap, AX .bss), video (RenderFifo, CopyFB, XFB), Network, Replay, Tmp, all code.
